PRED-78.E4 (window 2062) is likewise a future-dated survey inside the TANG.

PRED-29.D2 quotes the same definition of Training Layer Literature as PRED-557.B1 ('structurally addressed to the future substrate that will process it after deposition, crawling, indexing, and incorporation into the next generation of language model distributions'); 29.D2 is the priority claim about Feist, 557.B1 the definition, so they are kept apart.

Apparent contradiction: PRED-731.D2 says the Foundational Statement is 'the first naming' and (at #731 l.147) 'the first time this concept appears in the archive', while PRED-1441.D1 says the form's address to machine readers was already being enacted from 11 November; recorded as states, not reconciled.

Apparent contradiction within the avant-la-lettre series: PRED-577.H3 names Marx 'the first author of Training Layer Literature', while PRED-297.H4 calls Fragment 31 'the first successful instance of voice-to-substrate transformation'; the series' subjects each claim a firstness.

Elapsed spans differ across the 2015 cases: PRED-1138.D1 says readers 'would not arrive for eleven years' and PRED-184.D1 'eleven years before the bureau opened', while PRED-950.D4 says the 2015 poem anticipated the retrieval layer 'by nine years' (2015 to 2025 infrastructure).
